items.title: Lew Soloff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] We are filming at the Paradise Valley Jazz Party in Scottsdale, Arizona and my name is Monk Rowe. And it’s a great pleasure to have Lew Soloff with me... [INTERVIEWEE] Well thank you.

ctx.x: Trumpeter Lew Soloff was born in New York on February 20, 1944. He attended the Eastman School of Music and Juilliard, and was playing professionally in New York by the mid-1960’s. His versatility as a lead player and jazz soloist has enabled him to excel in big bands, small ensembles and in the commercial recording studios. Lew’s playing is well documented on recordings with Blood, Sweat & Tears, the Gil Evans Orchestra, the Manhattan Jazz Quintet and as a leader with his own ensembles.
Lew was interviewed in Scottsdale, Arizona on April 16, 2000, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.

We are filming at the Paradise Valley Jazz Party in Scottsdale, Arizona and my name is Monk Rowe. And it’s a great pleasure to have Lew Soloff with me, who is one of my favorite players. And I think when I look at your resume I’m trying to find someone who’s been doing more versatile work than you over the years. Difficult.
